data.cultural_impact: The name Vigneshwar is derived from the Tamil language and is an honorific title given to the Hindu deity, Lord Ganesha. In Hindu mythology, Lord Ganesha is known as the remover of obstacles and the patron of wisdom, knowledge, and education. Vigneshwar is also believed to be the lord of the threshold and the guardian of the doorways to temples and homes, making it an auspicious name to invoke for protection, prosperity, and wisdom.
data.spiritual_significance: Vigneshwar is an embodiment of wisdom, knowledge, and power. As the guardian of the spiritual path, he is said to guide and protect those who seek enlightenment and salvation. Vigneshwar represents the removal of obstacles that prevent spiritual growth and the attainment of wisdom and knowledge. In Hinduism, Vigneshwar is also considered the embodiment of the sacred syllable "OM," which is the sound of the universe and the origin of all creation. Hence, invoking the name Vigneshwar provides spiritual strength, guidance, and the removal of inner obstacles towards the path of Self-realization and ultimate salvation.

historical_references.reference:
According to mythology, Vigneshwar is considered to be the god of obstacles, remover of obstacles and the lord of all creations. He is the patron of the art of sculpture, and the god who blesses us with wisdom, knowledge and wealth. He is also known as the god of promise, grace, and success.
Context: Mythology and Hinduism
Time period: Ancient India

Vigneshwar is also known as Ganesha or Vinayak, the elephant-headed god. He is believed to have been born to the god Shiva and Goddess Parvati to protect her while she was bathing. He is often invoked at the beginning of any new venture or journey to remove any potential obstacles.
Context: Hindu rituals and practices
Time period: Medieval India

trends: God of obstacles and good fortune
